📄 Iran calls for expansion of regional mining cooperation

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The head of Iran Mining House has stressed the need to expand economic ties with regional countries, saying that boosting domestic mineral production and processing would help increase exports and strengthen Iran’s presence in regional markets.

Mohammad-Reza Bahraman made the remarks at the opening of the 20th International Exhibition of Mine, Mineral Industries, Mining Machinery and Equipment, Road Construction and Related Industries (IRAN CONMINE 2026), which began in Tehran on Wednesday.
​
The official described the exhibition as a major national event for the mining sector, providing a platform for exchanging expertise, expanding international cooperation and identifying new investment opportunities.
​
Bahraman said the country’s seventh development plan envisages 13% growth in the mining sector, adding that the exhibition would focus on practical ways to achieve the target and remove barriers to development.
​
The number of participants has increased by around 30% compared with the previous edition, with representatives from 36 countries expected to attend, he added.
​
The four-day exhibition opened with the participation of 128 domestic and foreign companies, including representatives from China, Japan, Russia, and India.

🎙 Iran says ready to help draft global treaty on plastic pollution

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Iran has declared its readiness to contribute effectively to drafting a global treaty to combat plastic pollution, stressing that the agreement must respect countries’ national circumstances, development rights, and capacities.

The announcement came during a meeting on the sidelines of the 17th Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17) in Yerevan, Armenia, between Hamid Zohrabi, deputy head of Iran’s Department of Environment for Natural Environment and Biodiversity, and officials involved in negotiations on the plastics treaty.
​
According to the Department of Environment’s public relations office, the meeting also involved the director general of the Foreign Ministry’s Department of International Organizations, the chair of the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee on Plastic Pollution and the executive secretary of its secretariat at the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP).
​
The Iranian delegation outlined Tehran’s national positions, emphasizing the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities and the need to protect countries’ right to development.
​
It also called for adequate and predictable financial resources, technology transfer, and capacity-building support for developing countries, warning against imposing uniform and unrealistic obligations on nations with different economic conditions and infrastructure.
​
The delegation underscored that the future treaty should adopt a realistic and implementable approach, allowing countries to choose measures suited to their national priorities and circumstances.
​
COP17 is being held in Yerevan from October 19 to 30, bringing together countries to assess progress under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework and discuss ways to accelerate conservation efforts, mobilize financial resources, and strengthen international cooperation.
